proposals.name: Vauntin Quell
proposals.entry:
First Citizen of Fogport, Lord Continuant, Protector of the Common Peace

For forty-three years, Vauntin Quell has ruled Fogport.

Before the Catastrophe, Quell was a minor royal minister responsible for emergency stores, civil preparedness, and public notices. When the royal family vanished during the destruction of the palace, Quell emerged from the smoke with soldiers, food wagons, printing presses—and a declaration granting himself emergency authority until order could be restored.

Order was restored.

The emergency never ended.

The Nice Man

Quell insists that he is approachable, reasonable, and fundamentally a very nice man.

During introductions, he smiles with his silver teeth and tells nervous visitors:

“Please. My friends call me Vaunt.”

Those who continue addressing him formally are sometimes chastised for their coldness. Those who accept the invitation eventually offend him by displaying insufficient respect.

They tend to disappear.

Quell never admits to taking offense. He merely expresses sadness that the person proved unworthy of his friendship.

The Silver Jaw

In the third year of his rule, an assassin shot Quell during a public address, destroying his lower jaw.

Quell remained standing long enough to issue orders for the assassin’s capture before collapsing. He reappeared months later with a polished mechanical silver jaw and a complete set of gleaming silver teeth.

He could disguise the injury, but prefers it conspicuous. The replacement transformed an attempted humiliation into a symbol of permanence.

Quell owns several interchangeable jaws:

  • A plain, severe jaw for trials and executions.
  • An ornate ceremonial jaw engraved with Fogport’s skyline.
  • A smiling jaw containing slightly too many silver teeth.
  • A blackened military jaw worn during emergencies.
  • Several additional designs that have never been shown publicly.

His attendants polish the selected jaw each morning and present it to him in a velvet-lined case.

The Seasonal Companions

Quell is frequently accompanied by a young and exceptionally beautiful woman introduced as his social secretary, cultural adviser, or official companion.

She is dressed magnificently, displayed at public ceremonies, and included in approved portraits. She rarely remains longer than a season.

Then she disappears.

Her rooms are emptied. Her likenesses are removed. Her family is discouraged from making inquiries. Another beautiful young woman soon occupies her place.

Some believe Quell somehow consumes their youth. Others suspect surgical experiments, private executions, or an attempt to recreate someone he lost during the Catastrophe.

Quell never mentions a former companion again.

The Falling of the Guard

The old City Guard initially supported Quell’s emergency government. When his temporary authority became permanent, its surviving officers demanded the restoration of lawful rule.

Quell accused the entire Guard of treason.

Its members were tried collectively in proceedings lasting less than two days. Officers and ordinary guardsmen alike were publicly guillotined in what became known as the Falling of the Guard.

Quell attended every execution wearing his plain silver jaw.

He then founded the Civic Vigilance.

The Civic Vigilance

The Vigilance are not merely police. They are Quell’s brownshirts: swaggering political enforcers who intimidate, beat, arrest, and disappear anyone judged insufficiently loyal.

Quell recruited them from street gangs, strikebreakers, failed soldiers, ambitious bullies, and people who enjoyed possessing authority but could never have earned it honorably. Their uniforms made thugs respectable without making them less thuggish.

They police sedition, unauthorized magic, public gatherings, labor unrest, criticism of Quell, and vaguely defined offenses against civic confidence. They are deliberately loud and conspicuous. Their brutality is part of their purpose.

Ordinary Fogport citizens fear the Civic Vigilance far more than they trust them.

Their founding maxim remains:

“The Guard watched the city. The Vigilance watches for it.”

The Face of Fogport

Quell’s likeness appears on coins, ration tins, tram tickets, government seals, schoolroom walls, official clocks, municipal machinery, and the prows of government vessels.

Enormous oil paintings depict him decades younger, taller, broader, healthier, and considerably more handsome than he ever was. Quell expects visitors to recognize these portraits without remarking upon their inaccuracies.

His most common emblem is a crude black stencil: swept-back hair, hollow eyes, and the unmistakable geometry of his silver jaw. Beneath it appears one command:

BEHOLD

Officially, citizens are instructed to behold what Fogport has survived.

Everyone understands that Vauntin Quell is also beholding them.

Damaging the image is prosecuted as the defacement of civic confidence.

The Cult of Continuance

Quell refuses the titles of king or emperor. He describes himself as a humble public servant burdened with permanent responsibility.

His preferred title is Lord Continuant—the man who ensured that Fogport continued.

Every year the city celebrates Continuance Day. Children wear paper silver jaws. Government employees listen to a ceremonial reading of Quell’s first emergency declaration. Lamps are lit beneath his portraits throughout the city.

Quell maintains an office devoted to collecting jokes, songs, graffiti, puppets, and unauthorized images concerning him. Clever mockery occasionally enters his private collection.

Poor likenesses offend him more than insults.

His Rule

Quell is a tyrant, but not a careless one.

The trams generally run. Grain reserves are maintained. Fires are fought. Trade continues. Monsters are contained whenever containment is economical.

His cruelty is usually bureaucratic. People disappear through revoked licenses, compulsory examinations, corrected addresses, midnight appointments, and transfers to departments that officially do not exist.

Quell genuinely believes Fogport would collapse without him.

After forty-three years, he may even be correct.

Whispers

No one knows how Vauntin Quell remains alive.

Some claim the public Quell is one of several surgically altered doubles. Others believe he stole something from beneath the royal palace during the Catastrophe. A few insist the original Quell died decades ago and his mechanical fittings are now doing most of the ruling.

The most dangerous rumor is that members of the former royal family survived—and that Quell has always known where they are.

posts.name: GAMEMASTER SECRETS — Vauntin Quell
posts.entry:
Do not establish the truth of these rumors until play reveals it.

Quell exploited the Catastrophe and may have helped cause or worsen the royal family’s destruction. His obsession with images may be more than vanity: he may believe that a sufficiently widespread and consistent public likeness preserves his identity against age, magic, or replacement.

Contradictory portraits genuinely distress him. The seasonal companions may be victims, experiments, doubles, or part of the same mechanism sustaining him. The fate of the royal family remains the most dangerous unanswered question of his reign.

Quell should remain intelligent, capable, peculiar, and occasionally correct. Fogport is more interesting if removing him could create consequences nearly as terrible as leaving him in power.
